enonce.texte: Match the infinitive form of the verb with its past simple form. Draw a line to connect them.

questions.texte: Match the verb forms
questions.reponse: go → went; eat → ate; see → saw; have → had; do → did; make → made; say → said; get → got

intitule: Fill in the Blank - Irregular Past

enonce.texte: Complete each sentence with the correct past simple form of the verb in parentheses. Choose from the irregular verbs you have learned.

questions.texte: Yesterday, I __________ (go) to the market with my mother.
questions.reponse: went

questions.texte: She __________ (eat) rice and fish for lunch.
questions.reponse: ate

questions.texte: We __________ (see) a beautiful bird in the garden.
questions.reponse: saw

questions.texte: He __________ (have) a headache yesterday.
questions.reponse: had

questions.texte: They __________ (do) their homework in the evening.
questions.reponse: did

questions.texte: My father __________ (make) a delicious cake for my birthday.
questions.reponse: made

enonce.texte:
Read the text about Paul's childhood. Then answer the questions using complete sentences in the past simple.

Paul's Childhood
When I was a child, I lived in a small village in Cameroon. I went to a primary school near my house. Every day, I walked to school with my friends. I ate breakfast at 7 a.m. I liked to play football after school. I saw many animals in the village. I had a dog named Max. My mother made delicious meals for us. I did not have a television, so I read books.

questions.texte: Where did Paul live when he was a child?
questions.reponse: He lived in a small village in Cameroon.

questions.texte: What did Paul eat for breakfast?
questions.reponse: He ate breakfast at 7 a.m.

questions.texte: Did Paul play football after school?
questions.reponse: Yes, he played football after school.

questions.texte: What was the name of Paul's dog?
questions.reponse: His dog was named Max.

questions.texte: Why did Paul read books?
questions.reponse: He read books because he did not have a television.

enonce.texte: Transform the following affirmative sentences into negative sentences in the past simple.

questions.texte: I went to school yesterday.
questions.reponse: I didn't go to school yesterday.

questions.texte: She ate rice for dinner.
questions.reponse: She didn't eat rice for dinner.

questions.texte: We saw a movie last night.
questions.reponse: We didn't see a movie last night.

questions.texte: He had a car in 2020.
questions.reponse: He didn't have a car in 2020.

questions.texte: They made a cake for the party.
questions.reponse: They didn't make a cake for the party.

enonce.texte: Form questions in the past simple for the following sentences. Use the question word in parentheses (if provided) or form a yes/no question.

questions.texte: She went to Douala. (Where)
questions.reponse: Where did she go?

questions.texte: He ate fish for lunch. (What)
questions.reponse: What did he eat for lunch?

questions.texte: They saw a doctor yesterday. (Who)
questions.reponse: Who did they see yesterday?

questions.texte: You made a mistake. (Did...?)
questions.reponse: Did you make a mistake?

questions.texte: She had a good time at the party. (Did...?)
questions.reponse: Did she have a good time at the party?

enonce.texte: Write a short paragraph (5-8 sentences) about your childhood. Use at least five irregular verbs in the past simple. You can talk about where you lived, what you liked to do, your friends, your family, or your favorite activities.

questions.texte: Write your childhood story.
questions.reponse: When I was a child, I lived in Bamenda. I went to primary school near my home. I liked to play with my friends after school. I ate a lot of fruits like mangoes and bananas. I had a bicycle and I rode it everywhere. My mother made delicious food for us. I saw many interesting things in the village. I did not have a smartphone, so I played outside every day.

enonce.texte:
Work with a partner. Interview your classmate about his/her childhood. Ask at least five questions. Then write the answers in complete sentences. Use the past simple tense.

Example questions:

  • Where did you live when you were a child?
  • What did you like to do after school?
  • Did you have a pet?
  • What did you eat for breakfast?
  • Who was your best friend?

questions.texte: Write the questions you asked and your partner's answers.
questions.reponse: Q1: Where did you live when you were a child? A1: I lived in Yaoundé. Q2: What did you like to do after school? A2: I liked to play football with my friends. Q3: Did you have a pet? A3: Yes, I had a cat. Q4: What did you eat for breakfast? A4: I ate bread and drank tea. Q5: Who was your best friend? A5: My best friend was Jean.
